title: spec: QueryTransportParamsSchema.select / $select and GetDataRequestSchema.select admit an empty projection that the findData and getData doors refuse (sibling of #26817)
body:
Filing gate: ① a declaration wider than the door it declares. Found while landing #26817 (PR #26901): the dev's os-dev-report on #26817 (6452436506, out-of-scope findings, class b) and the contract review on PR #26901 (6452937369, ① 5 and ③). Filed by `domain:spec` seat 3 · `os-support-ai` · session `session_01WGufzgbJhFoXYsLSe5WSPP`. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets lane and grade (spec lane suggested).

**Business reason.** A generated client, a docs reader or an AI author trusts the published schema. Where the schema admits an empty projection and the door answers 400, the caller learns the rule only at runtime. PR #26901 fixed this for the GET querystring (`HttpFindQueryParamsSchema.select`); the two sibling declarations of the same rule still admit it. After #26901 lands, two declarations of the one `findData` door also disagree on `select` (one strict, one loose).

## Measured (origin/main, read in the review of PR #26901)

1. **`findData` door, body side.** `QueryTransportParamsSchema.select` (`z.union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])`) and `$select` in `packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts` admit `''`, a whitespace/comma-only string and `[]`. The door (`projectionFieldsValue`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` ~:4645, reached via `options.fields` ~:12996) splits on commas, trims, drops empties and refuses an empty result with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming `select` (since #26811). Readers of this declaration: `QueryWithTransportSchema`, `FindDataRequestSchema.query`, the `POST /data/:object/query` body, the RPC alias table and `QuerySchema.fields`.
2. **`getData` door (by id).** `GetDataRequestSchema.select: z.array(z.string())` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` ~:2407) admits `[]`; the door refuses it through the same `projectionFieldsValue(request.select, 'select')` (~:13576).

## Wanted (the spec seat decides the shape)

Both declarations admit exactly what their door accepts: at least one field name after the door's own split/trim (PR #26901's `/[^\s,]/` rule is provably equivalent to the door for a string; an array needs at least one non-blank member, as the door judges it). Measure each reader listed above and keep `.describe()` texts true. Schema tests pin `''`, `' , '` and `[]` as refused and a normal list as accepted, on each declaration.

**Clause-②:** likely `no (narrowing)`, measured by the dev. **Metadata-protocol:** likely `none` (transport declarations, as ruled for #26817), measured by the dev. ADR-0087: likely `not-required` (no stored rows).
